comparisons.peer_summary: The company has a long history of operating in Asia, where it manufactures and sources the majority of its products and materials, and stores the majority of its product inventory in a warehouse in Malaysia.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom (AVGO) highlight their manufacturing presence in Asia, though with different strategic emphases. Intel lists specific assembly and testing facilities in China, Malaysia, and Vietnam, and wafer facilities in Ireland and Israel, as part of a global network intended to build the majority of products internally. Broadcom notes a long history of operating in Asia where it manufactures and sources the majority of its products, storing the majority of inventory in Malaysia to stay close to customer manufacturing facilities. While both utilize Asian facilities for manufacturing/sourcing, Intel emphasizes its broad global footprint including US/Ireland/Israel wafer sites and internal building intent, whereas Broadcom emphasizes its historical reliance on Asia for the majority of manufacturing and sourcing.

sentences.text: We operate wafer manufacturing facilities in the United States (Oregon and Arizona), Ireland, and Israel, assembly and testing facilities in Costa Rica, China, Malaysia, and Vietnam, and packaging facilities in the United States (New Mexico), Costa Rica, Vietnam, and Malaysia.
We intend to remain a leading developer of process technology and a major manufacturer of semiconductors and we plan to continue to build the majority of our products in our factories.
We also have a long history of operating in Asia where we manufacture and source the majority of our products and materials.
We store the majority of our product inventory in our warehouse in Malaysia and our presence in Asia places us in close proximity to many of our customers' manufacturing facilities.

comparisons.peer_topic: Global manufacturing footprint and subcontractor use
comparisons.peer_summary: Products are manufactured in own facilities across seven countries and utilize subcontractors for certain processes.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose operating a global network of owned manufacturing facilities across multiple countries, emphasizing direct control over production. Intel specifies wafer, assembly, testing, and packaging sites in the US, Ireland, Israel, Costa Rica, China, Malaysia, and Vietnam, intending to build the majority of products in its own factories. Similarly, Micron manufactures products in its own facilities in Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, the US, Malaysia, China, and India, noting that while it utilizes subcontractors for certain processes, the core manufacturing footprint is owned and global. Both companies highlight their extensive geographic spread and internal capacity as key operational features, contrasting with fabless peers.

sentences.text: We operate wafer manufacturing facilities in the United States (Oregon and Arizona), Ireland, and Israel, assembly and testing facilities in Costa Rica, China, Malaysia, and Vietnam, and packaging facilities in the United States (New Mexico), Costa Rica, Vietnam, and Malaysia.
We intend to remain a leading developer of process technology and a major manufacturer of semiconductors and we plan to continue to build the majority of our products in our factories.

We manufacture our products within our own facilities located in Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, the United States, Malaysia, China, and India and also utilize subcontractors to perform certain manufacturing processes.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fabless manufacturing strategy and cost benefits
comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA utilizes a fabless and contracting manufacturing strategy, employing partners for wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging to avoid significant costs and risks associated with owning manufacturing operations. This approach allows the company to focus resources on product design, quality assurance, marketing, and customer support.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and NVIDIA present fundamentally opposite strategies regarding manufacturing ownership. Intel explicitly states its intention to remain a major manufacturer and build the majority of its products in its own factories, leveraging its global factory network for product optimization and supply resilience. In contrast, NVIDIA utilizes a fabless strategy, employing partners for all phases of manufacturing including wafer fabrication, assembly, and packaging to avoid the significant costs and risks associated with owning manufacturing operations. This contrast highlights Intel's integrated model versus NVIDIA's asset-light approach.

sentences.text: Our global factory network has been foundational to our success, enabling product optimization, improved economics, and supply resilience.
We intend to remain a leading developer of process technology and a major manufacturer of semiconductors and we plan to continue to build the majority of our products in our factories.

We utilize a fabless and contracting manufacturing strategy, whereby we employ and partner with key suppliers for all phases of the manufacturing process, including wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging.
Additionally, we can avoid many of the significant costs and risks associated with owning and operating manufacturing operations.

comparisons.peer_summary: QCT primarily uses a fabless production model, relying on third parties for manufacturing, assembly, and testing of integrated circuits, with suppliers located mainly in the Asia-Pacific region. Primary foundry suppliers include TSMC, Global Foundries, Samsung, and SMIC, while primary assembly and test suppliers include ASE, Amkor, SPI, and STATSChipPAC.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and Qualcomm differ significantly in their reliance on internal versus third-party manufacturing. Intel describes its global factory network as foundational, intending to build the majority of its products in its own facilities to ensure supply resilience. Conversely, Qualcomm (specifically its QCT segment) primarily uses a fabless production model, meaning it does not own foundries for silicon wafer production and instead relies on third parties for manufacturing, assembly, and testing. While Qualcomm uses internal facilities for specific RFFE products, its general model is distinct from Intel's integrated manufacturing approach.

sentences.text: Our global factory network has been foundational to our success, enabling product optimization, improved economics, and supply resilience.
We intend to remain a leading developer of process technology and a major manufacturer of semiconductors and we plan to continue to build the majority of our products in our factories.

Other than for certain of our RFFE modules and RF filter products, QCT utilizes a fabless production model, which means that we do not own or operate foundries for the production of silicon wafers from which our integrated circuits are made.

Therefore, we primarily rely on third parties to perform the manufacturing and assembly, and most of the testing, of our integrated circuits based primarily on our proprietary designs and test programs.
